detailed_description: The Stacked Bar Chart Generator transforms multi-dimensional datasets into interactive visualizations that reveal part-to-whole relationships across categorical axes. Built on a D3.js rendering engine, this tool encodes quantitative values through proportional segment heights within composite bars, enabling comparative analysis of subcategory contributions to total values. Developers and data analysts use this tool to decode complex distributions in sales pipelines, resource allocation models, or demographic surveys where layered data comparison is critical. The generator accepts structured input formats like CSV/TSV/JSON, automatically parsing numerical fields into stackable series while preserving axis labeling integrity. Users can specify normalization parameters to convert absolute values into percentage-based representations, with advanced options for axis inversion, logarithmic scaling, and CSS-driven color encoding. Client-side WebAssembly processing ensures real-time rendering of datasets containing up to 10,000 data points with hardware-accelerated canvas updates.
usage_steps: Import structured data via drag-and-drop CSV/TSV file upload or paste raw text into the syntax-highlighted editor panel
Map columns to 'Base Category' (X-axis) and 'Stack Series' (segment components) using the schema mapping interface
Configure stacking behavior in the Calculation Panel: choose between absolute value stacking or percentage normalization
Customize visual encoding through the Style Inspector: assign divergent color scales, adjust bar spacing, and enable data labels
Activate interactive preview mode to test responsiveness across breakpoint thresholds for mobile/tablet/desktop displays
Export production-ready SVG/PNG renderings with embedded metadata or copy generated D3/Chart.js code snippets for web integration
usage_examples: A marketing analyst visualizing quarterly ad spend allocation across channels (social, email, search) for three regional markets, comparing campaign composition efficiency
Public health researchers displaying vaccination rate breakdowns by age group across five municipalities using normalized percentage stacks
Renewable energy engineers comparing daily power generation mix (solar, wind, hydro) against total grid demand over a 30-day period
University administrators analyzing student enrollment distributions across four academic colleges (STEM, humanities, business, arts) by undergraduate/graduate status
